title: Chapter 41: Hold Your Breath
html:
“Specters’ Favored, your courage is admirable. This Nightmare Mission is both a test and a reward!

“The mission is called ‘Deep Water.’ It is said to bring the boundary between the living and the dead close enough for you to glimpse someone who has passed beyond it.

“Mission Requirement: At the appointed hour, enter the designated bathroom alone and follow the ritual displayed by the black phone. The ritual uses darkness, water, and a single light as symbolic points between Yin and Yang. Do not attempt it outside the mission.

“When night gives way to dawn, the boundary between the two worlds is said to be at its thinnest.

“The mission will be complete if the ritual produces a vision of the person you wish to see. If no vision appears, remain until the black phone confirms completion.”

Chen Ge read the description twice. Compared with his first Nightmare Mission, this one looked shorter and less complicated—but that only made him more suspicious.

A Nightmare Mission had never been simple merely because its instructions were brief.

The setting is another bathroom, but this time the black phone is asking me to complete some kind of water ritual. There has to be more to it than the description says.

He studied the requirements carefully. The ritual itself would not take long, yet the black phone’s warning made it impossible to dismiss the danger.

What truly caught Chen Ge’s attention was one line in the description: “bring the boundary between the living and the dead close enough for you to glimpse someone who has passed beyond it.”

Unlike most people, Chen Ge tended to become calmer under pressure. Sitting alone, he considered the possibilities. His parents had disappeared at an abandoned hospital in the countryside, leaving behind only a doll and the black phone. The phone had activated just as he was preparing to give up the Haunted House, and during the first Nightmare Mission, the doll they had left him had protected him. Could both objects have been deliberately left as clues?

If so, the second Nightmare Mission might contain more than a reward.

Maybe this is another way for them to leave me information.

It was only speculation. Even so, Chen Ge knew he would accept the mission regardless. He had too many unanswered questions to ignore a lead this direct.

Bring the boundary between the living and the dead close enough for you to glimpse someone who has passed beyond it.

To Chen Ge, the promise carried a painful possibility. If his parents did not appear, perhaps that meant they were still alive somewhere. If they did, then the black phone might truly have been left behind as a message—or even as a final path for him to follow.

I can’t walk away from this.

Chen Ge checked the time. The appointed hour was approaching.I spent too long dealing with those mirrors. I need to move.

The only bathroom in the Haunted House that matched the mission’s description was the one connected to Murder by Midnight through the workers’ passage—the same concealed route Chen Ge used when operating the scenario.

There’s no time to find another suitable location. I’ll have to do it here, right in the mirror entity’s territory.

Once the decision was made, Chen Ge gathered the four dolls and prepared the bathroom as the black phone required, keeping everything he might need for the Haunted House close at hand.

If that thing appears again, I’m not facing it alone.

He checked the room twice, more for reassurance than anything else. The dolls were in place, the recording phone was ready, and the workers’ passage remained clear behind him.

By the time he finished, the appointed hour was close.

Everything is ready. Now I find out what this mission really is.

With the front entrance to Murder by Midnight locked, Chen Ge entered the bathroom through the workers’ passage. He was alone, as the mission required. The mirror he had broken earlier lay in scattered fragments across the floor.

I made enough noise preparing the room that the mirror entity probably knows I’m here. All the more reason to stay alert.

On paper, the mission seemed strange rather than dangerous. Chen Ge trusted that impression less with every passing second.

He secured the bathroom door and placed the doll left by his parents nearby. The four rag dolls associated with Ping An Apartments were arranged around the room as an extra precaution.

“I may need your help again,” he told them quietly. “Don’t let anything sneak up on me.”

As before, he set his phone to record and positioned it where the room would remain in frame. In the near-total darkness, the preview showed little more than a vague silhouette.

When the black phone signaled him to begin, Chen Ge followed the ritual’s remaining prompts. A small flame became the room’s only steady light, multiplying itself across the mirror fragments on the floor.

A chill seemed to spread through the bathroom. The water in the tub trembled although the room was still, and its dark surface looked deeper than the shallow basin had any right to be.

This mission is seriously unsettling.

Chen Ge settled beside the tub and kept his attention on the black phone. As the ritual activated, the reflected candlelight distorted, and the room seemed to tilt away from him.

That is definitely not normal.

The air turned unnaturally cold. One moment Chen Ge was sitting in the bathroom; the next, his senses told him he was sinking through dark water even though he had not moved.

Just get through the ritual. Then I’ll have my answer.

He forced himself to remain calm and waited for the black phone’s next signal.
